title: What is England's route to World Cup final and what knockout stage bracket are they in? | talkSPORT
text:
Thomas Tuchel's England beat DR Congo 2-1 in the Round of 32 and were rescued by captain Harry Kane, who scored a stunning double to complete a brilliant comeback.

More drama followed in the last-16 last Sunday night with a thrilling 3-2 victory over co-hosts Mexico at the Azteca Stadium.

England are now into the semi-finals after beating Norway and there was yet more excitement in Miami.

Jude Bellingham was the hero, firing home twice as the Three Lions won in extra-time.

With the Croatia, Ghana, and Panama group games done, Tuchel's side have beaten DR Congo and Mexico in the knockout rounds.

They then needed extra-time to turn around their clash with Norway and beat them 2-1 to make the semi-finals.

England are in the lower bracket of the World Cup and will take on Argentina next.

The Three Lions will have taken great heart from eliminating Mexico and Norway.

The semi-final against holders Argentina will take place at 8pm UK time on Wednesday, July 15.

And should England get to the final, they would return to the MetLife on July 19 at 8pm UK time.

They would face a team in the top bracket of the tournament which now only includes France and Spain.

Should England lose in the semi-finals, there is a third place play off at this summer's tournament.

Group Stage

Knockout Stage

England head coach Thomas Tuchel wasn't happy with the performance against Norway but hailed his main man.

He said: "We made life very, very difficult for ourselves today. The result is fantastic, we're in the last four. It's amazing. I'm not happy with the performance.

"In every sense. The commitment is there but we made life very, very difficult for us in the way we played, how we played. Sloppy, tactical mistakes, not fast enough. Not repetitive enough. We were lucky enough.

"Mentality? This [getting through] is pure mentality now. How can you talk about mentality now? This is pure mentality.

"It's not a mentality problem. You can bottle it up and sell it. Why are you talking about mentality.

"It's the quality of our game [that's the problem]. It's about quality, we need to play better."

On Bellingham, Tuchel added: "Enough said, he does it every match. World class."

"We will get better, we need to get better. Now it's celebrations. Now it's taking it all in. We need everything to make a better performance."
